best_for: App and web developers who need to see, and sometimes change, the HTTP and HTTPS traffic between their code, phones or emulators and a server.
description:
Proxyman is an HTTP and HTTPS debugging proxy made by Proxyman LLC. It sits between your apps and the servers they talk to and decrypts HTTPS so every request and response shows in plain text, grouped by app and domain.

You can pause a request at a breakpoint and edit its headers or body before it goes on, answer a call with a local file instead of the real server, compare two requests side by side, and build new requests from scratch or from a pasted cURL command. It reads WebSocket messages and GraphQL queries, captures traffic from iPhones, Android phones, simulators and emulators, and has a built-in MCP server so AI tools such as Claude Code can read and work with the captured traffic.

points.title: Free to try, paid for the real tools
points.text: The free trial captures and previews traffic. Its comparison table marks Breakpoint, Map Local, Map Remote, Scripting, Diff, multiple filters, WebSocket preview, HAR import and MCP as paid, and limits debugging rules to one.

points.title: One-time licenses with a year of updates
points.text: At the time of reading, Standard was USD 89 for one device and Personal was USD 99 for two devices plus the iOS and Android apps, shown with a Black Friday discount. Both are one-time purchases with a year of updates; after that you keep the last version you got. Team licenses start at five seats, a yearly subscription adds cloud features, and students can ask for 50% off.

points.title: One license for every desktop system
points.text: A seat covers one Mac, Windows or Linux computer at a time, and you can move it to a new computer by deactivating the old one.

points.title: The Mac app is ahead
points.text: The Mac version is a native app with its own version numbers, and some features are Mac only, such as HTTP/2 capture and the Network Extension beta for macOS 26. At the time of this listing, macOS was on 26.6.1 and Windows on 26.3.0.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 14 or later
points.text: The Homebrew cask installs one universal disk image for Intel and Apple silicon Macs, for macOS 14 Sonoma and newer, and adds the proxyman-cli command.

points.title: Windows: x64, installed for one user
points.text: Proxyman lists Windows 10 and 11. The installer is x64 only and installs for the current user, not machine-wide.

points.title: Linux builds exist, but not here
points.text: Proxyman offers an AppImage and a .deb for Ubuntu and Debian. It is not on Flathub, and this listing covers Windows and Mac only.

points.title: Old versions on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 49 versions. macOS lists only the current release, so an older Mac build has to come from Proxyman.
